source_text:
Περὶ μὲν τῶν ἀνηκόντων τῇ θρησκείᾳ ἡμῶν καὶ τῶν ὠφελιμωτάτων εἰς ἐνάρετον βίον τοῖς θέλουσιν εὐσεβῶς καὶ δικαίως διευθύνειν, ἱκανῶς ἐπεστείλαμεν ὑμῖν, ἄνδρες ἀδελφοί.
περὶ γὰρ πίστεως καὶ μετανοίας καὶ γνησίας ἀγάπης καὶ ἐγκρατείας καὶ σωφροσύνης καὶ ὑπομονῆς πάντα τόπον ἐψηλαφήσαμεν, ὑπομιμνήσκοντες δεῖν ὑμᾶς ἐν δικαιοσύνῃ καὶ ἀληθείᾳ καὶ μακροθυμίᾳ τῷ παντοκράτορι θεῷ ὁσίως εὐαρεστεῖν, ὁμονοοῦντας ἀμνησικάκως ἐν ἀγάπῃ καὶ εἰρήνῃ μετὰ ἐκτενοῦς ἐπιεικείας, καθὼς καὶ οἱ προδεδηλωμένοι πατέρες ἡμῶν εὐηρέστησαν ταπεινοφρονοῦντες τὰ πρὸς τὸν πατέρα καὶ κτίστην θεὸν καὶ πάντας ἀνθρώπους.
καὶ ταῦτα τοσούτῳ ἥδιον ὑπεμνήσαμεν, ἐπειδὴ σαφῶς ᾔδειμεν γράφειν ἡμᾶς ἀνδράσιν πιστοῖς καὶ ἐλλογιμωτάτοις καὶ ἐγκεκυφόσιν εἰς τὰ λόγια τῆς παιδείας τοῦ θεοῦ.
thought_title: The letter's summary of its own teaching
orientation: The Roman church is closing its letter to Corinth by summarizing what it has written about faith, repentance, love, and the virtues, and why it wrote to such faithful and learned men.
pass_a_gloss: Concerning the things that pertain to our religion and the things most helpful for a virtuous life for those who wish to direct themselves piously and justly, we have written to you sufficiently, men and brothers. For concerning faith and repentance and genuine love and self-control and sound-mindedness and endurance we have touched on every topic, reminding you that you must in righteousness and truth and patience please the almighty God holily, being of one mind without remembering wrongs in love and peace with earnest gentleness, just as also our previously mentioned fathers pleased him, being humble in the things toward the Father and Creator God and toward all people. And these things we reminded you of all the more gladly, since we knew clearly that we were writing to faithful and most distinguished men who have diligently examined the oracles of the instruction of God.

choices.why: The verb means to feel or handle; in this context it means to treat or touch upon topics, so 'touched on' preserves the tactile metaphor while fitting the sense of covering every topic.
The compound means 'not remembering evils'; a literal rendering keeps the force of the adverb rather than collapsing it into a single abstract noun.
The perfect participle of ἐγκύπτω means to stoop or bend down to look into something; the literal posture conveys the attentive study of Scripture.
Λόγια refers to divine utterances or sayings; 'oracles' preserves the sacred, spoken character of the term.
Παιδεία means training or discipline; 'instruction' fits the context of God's formative teaching.

pass_b_english: Brothers, we have written to you at length about the matters that belong to our religion and are most useful for a virtuous life to those who wish to guide their course piously and justly.

We have touched on every topic: faith, repentance, genuine love, self-control, sound-mindedness, and endurance. We reminded you that you must please almighty God in holiness, with righteousness, truth, and patience. You must live in harmony, holding no memory of wrongs, in love and peace with earnest gentleness. This is how our fathers mentioned earlier pleased him: they showed humility toward God the Father and Creator, and toward all people.

We reminded you of these things all the more gladly because we knew clearly that we were writing to faithful and most distinguished men, men who have diligently examined the oracles of God's instruction.

problems.why: ἐγκεκυφόσιν means 'stooped over, peered into, examined closely'—a posture of diligent study, not 'bent down into' which suggests submission or physical bowing.
Not a glossary violation per se, but 'self-control' already used for ἐγκρατείας; σωφροσύνη is 'sober-mindedness' or 'prudence.' However, no glossary entry exists for this term.

edits.old: who have bent down into the oracles of God's instruction
edits.new: who have diligently examined the oracles of God's instruction

fixed: sound-mindedness: no glossary entry exists for σωφροσύνης, and the English already renders it as 'sound-mindedness,' which is a standard translation; no change made.

polish.changed: Broke the long opening sentence into clearer units, made the implied subject 'we' explicit, clarified the antecedent of 'him' as God, and restructured the final clause so the readers are described naturally rather than in a tangled participial phrase.

Clarified the implied subject of the second paragraph, broke the long sentence into shorter natural units, and made the connection between the Corinthians' required conduct and the example of the fathers explicit.

last_rejected.quote: we have written to you at length
last_rejected.why: ἱκανῶς means sufficiently or enough, not that the letter was long or detailed.
last_rejected.fix: Brothers, we have written enough to you about the matters that belong to our religion
last_rejected.ruling: ἱκανῶς ἐπεστείλαμεν means 'we have written sufficiently/adequately'; 'at length' is a close, acceptable rendering within range, not a change in meaning.
